artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: PacedSession.get now appends {url, status, body, fetched_at} to self.captured for every response it returns or raises on (captured BEFORE the status-code raise branches). Exercised by AC1's test_paced_session_captures_response_bytes and every article/listing raw_bytes arm.

normalize() gains raw_url; Publisher gains .listings (reset at articles()) and ._record_listing (defensive: no-ops on a session with no .captured ledger, so a bare stub session never crashes); seeking_alpha now fetches each new article's own response for raw_bytes/raw_ext/raw_url; bloomberg captures raw_bytes/raw_ext/raw_url off the article response and records a listing entry per search page; financial_times and DowJones.article (wsj/barrons) carry raw_bytes/raw_ext/raw_url off the actual response object; dow_jones records one listing entry per discover() call.

put_article_bronze takes received_form (default as_received; refused via ValueError before any store call if not in {as_received, normalised_record}) and writes it as bronze metadata; new listing_query_hash (sha256 hex of the UTF-8 query) and put_listing_bronze (dedupes on the query_hash_p{page}_ prefix under date=<fetch date>, writes received-form: as_received).

harvest_listing_outbox table added (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, always, matching the existing harvest_raw_outbox pattern); _write_harvest_raw now also stores raw_url in its record_json (not an ARTICLE_FIELDS member, added explicitly since catalog.py is out of this cell's surface); new _write_harvest_listings stages each Publisher.listings entry to a local file plus a harvest_listing_outbox row; called from run_job in harvest mode only (config key harvest_grammar), right after the article loop completes.

HarvestUploader.run splits into _run_articles (unchanged logic, moved) and new _run_listings (puts pending harvest_listing_outbox rows through harvest_grammar.put_listing_bronze); _has_listing_table guards both the dispatch and the remaining_pending count so a db lacking the newer table (test_harvest_grammar.py's manual :memory: db) is unaffected. _run_articles calls put_article_bronze WITHOUT an explicit received_form kwarg (relies on the function's own as_received default) -- see surprise AMGT_HARVST-Z-W1-S1.

New file, 12 arms exactly as section 1 item 6 names them, over STUB inner sessions (curl_cffi-shaped fake responses returned in a fixed order) and a STUB S3 client (same shape as lib/research/harvest/tests/test_store.py's _StubS3). No network, no vendor call, no live bucket, no AWS credential use. Each raw_bytes arm's stub body is deliberately non-canonical (extra spaces / non-sorted keys) so a re-serialization of the parsed value would fail the arm -- demonstrated live by the mutant control (see controls.mutant).
